\parbox{\columnwidth}{\scriptsize Batch size 1, Avenue test frames at 640$\times$360, RTX 3090 GPU and AMD EPYC 7542 CPU, PyTorch 2.4.1. Each run: 20 warm-up frames, then 3$\times$100 timed frames; each value is the median of the per-repetition medians over 1, 3 and 4 runs (columns left to right). TensorRT 10.3.0 FP16 engines for the two YOLO11n models; the image encoder stays in PyTorch because its TensorRT engine changed the embeddings (mean cosine 0.947 to the reference embeddings over 481 crops). On the Ped1 development set the TensorRT detectors change the online micro AUC by $+$0.19 (object branch) and $+$0.05 (object + grid) points; on the test sets by Ped2 $-$0.04\,/\,$-$0.01, Avenue $+$0.46\,/\,$+$0.62, ShT $-$0.31\,/\,$-$0.09 (object branch / object + grid); Avenue object + grid exceeds the pre-registered margin of 0.5. All accuracy numbers in this paper use the PyTorch detectors. With PyTorch limited to 4 threads: 12.5 FPS sequential, 18.3 FPS with parallel flow. The host was shared (1-min load average 11.63--32.69, recorded before and after the runs). Par.\ flow: the optical flow runs in a CPU thread, in parallel with the GPU stages. $^{a}$Time the main loop waits for the flow thread. $^{b}$Measured per frame; it includes steps not listed (cropping, attribute computation), so the stage values do not add up to it.}
